materials.content:
Watercolor on moderately thick, cream, rough wove paper; Watermark: ANCNE MANUFRE CANSON & MONTGOLFIER VIDALON-LES-ANNONAY A LAVIS
(Source: Paper Survey researched by Judith C. Walsh and published in Lynes, 1999.)

cr_data.provenance: Private collection, Harper Woods, Minnesota, purchase, 1976; Frank E. Fowler, Lookout Mountain, Tennessee, c. 1976; (Helene Wasserman Fine Art, New York, NY); Joshua Strychalski, New York, NY, 1977; Davis & Langdale Company, Inc., New York, NY, 1977; Joshua Strychalski, New York, NY, 1980; (Middendorf Gallery, Washington, DC) (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive. Work inspired by first of several visits O'Keeffe made to York Beach, Maine, in the 1920s. See cat. nos. 325, 326, 381–387, 440, 441, 604. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999: Lynes publication dates this work as 1920. High Museum of Art dates it as 1922. (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* from High Museum of Art, 2025)

titles.title: Seaweed No. II

credit_line: High Museum of Art, Atlanta; Gift of Lily Friedlander
description: A cluster of seaweed in shades of burgundy, dark green, pink, and gray sits in the center of the composition, surrounded by plain white paper. The varying varieties of seaweed are all delicately painted and intertwine with one another.
imageCaption: Courtesy of High Museum of Art.
title: Seaweed No. II
